newsitem.title: KENYA: African leaders start Zaire crisis meeting.
newsitem.headline: African leaders start Zaire crisis meeting.

text.p: African leaders opened a meeting in Nairobi on Wednesday on the Zaire crisis with a strong call for negotiations to end the war tearing apart Zaire.

Host Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi told the presidents of Zimbabwe and Congo, South Africa's deputy president and representatives from Cameroon that failure to end the conflict would lead to "far and wide" repercussions.
"The deteriorating situation in Zaire calls for all our energies to check it to avoid further bloodshed and human suffering," Moi told leaders including Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo.
"At this stage, and taking into account the latest developments, I can see that a negotiated settlement is necessary in order to arrive at a lasting solution," he added.

Before the start of the Nairobi meeting, South African Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo and European Union special envoy Aldo Ajello said they hoped for a ceasefire in Zaire to pave the way for a political settlement.

In Nairobi for the meeting are Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe, Congolese President Pascal Lissouba, South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki and representatives of Cameroon, the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity (OAU).
